This a fun Hidden Object Game (HOG for short). Not a Puzzle HOG, but a true and pure HOG. it is a lot of fun. 

However: The places you have to search are a 360 degree view, and there is a good reason most HOGs avoid this and the reason is a simple one most would not understand-unless they have experienced it first hand and that reason is: Motion sickness. 

Yep, you read that right. Motion sickness. This is because unlike static image HOGs, you are focusing on a certain section but also moving the view, for those who are prone to motion sickness will need to either pass or play this game in short bursts. if you do not suffer this issue, then you should have no problems at but for those who do, consider this fair warning before you buy.

It's an ok HOG only game with only one major bug I could find...

So, the story is a bit convoluted, and it's mostly conveyed with a bit of text story and dialogue between characters. Something about different timelines, ancient alien symbols, in a mix and mash of things I couldn't fully understand. You and your team/family has to find all of these symbols in different timelines to input all of it into an ancient alien time machine of sorts of stabilize all the timlines.

Anyways, back to mechanics. This is a HOG only game, no puzzles, no other mechanics. You basically have to find a whole bunch of items in a given scenario. The difference between this game and the better known Artifex Mundi games for instance, is that you have a 360 look on scene.
Lots of people might not like this, because the objects are not contained in a single scene, you have to keep looking around to find them.

There are three variants for the hidden object scenes - the prevalent one is the classic word matching, there are also a few object matching, and a few find two copies of the same object.

There's a scene that appears after playing the game a bit in which you have to match masks... for whatever reason I completed this part some 3 times with the last object not triggering the end sequence for the scene. On the 4th time I played the whole scene I left the main object, a red-ish mask, to find last, and then it triggered the end sequence.

Anyways, it's somewhat on the same level of the earliest HOG games... I still found it plenty enjoyable.

While it's not the greatest, I still recommend this as it's exactly what it says it is: a free hidden objects game; and, if that's what you're looking for, you'll definitely find it here. I was a bit concerned going in as it froze up on me the first time I tried to play it and some reviewers stated they were having trouble with it loading and receiving achievements. After the initial hiccup though, I had no issues with it running and all the achievements unlocked fine. 

As for the game itself, there is a story line, but it was really hard to follow as, even though it says 'tap to continue', it will just load the next screen after a short period anyways so I was often unable to fully read and comprehend everything. You don't need to know the story to play the game of course, but it was rather annoying. Also, while the game description might proclaim "amazing graphics" or whatever, the whole thing is extremely cartoonish and child-like, which made certain objects beyond easy to spot. Another thing many people mentioned was the energy limit or whatever that prevents you from playing straight through. Sure, I can understand that could be annoying to some, but it's also a free game and these types of games are better played in small spurts anyways, so it didn't really bother me. I finished the whole thing in about 4 hours over a couple days. 

Lastly, the hidden object aspect of the game. Despite all of the above, I found it enjoyable. The same group of locations were used multiple times to follow the different characters and basically included all the objects for each level all at once. That, mixed with a nice depth of field instead of a flat surface and some well hidden objects made certain bits easy and certain parts more difficult. All in all, despite its shortcomings, it is free and a fun little hidden object game for when you're in the mood.

[h1]The real mystery here is...why the hell did I download this game?![/h1]

Okay, to be honest, I did not like this one.  Sure, [i]Mystery Island - Hidden Object Games[/i] is a 360 hidden object game, but the music is bad, maps are annoying, and items that you need to grab (along with useless garbage that are really only important to different character missions of the same location) seem to just be images stuck in from stock sources.  I played this for one hour before putting it down...heck, on the very first puzzle, what the game doesn't tell you is that a few objects are translucent...that's pretty low.  I get that they are supposed to blend in, but when you throw transparency into the mix, then there's a problem.  Fortunately, this is mostly for the first few missions and it returns again around the end.

If we were to talk about the story...I were to say it's complete garbage.  It keeps jumping between flashbacks of the parents with the grandfather and the present with the daughter being told the story of her parents by her grandfather... in about 2 sentence dialogues for your cutscenes.  "Your parents were here too" "Great, let's go find dad's balls!"...for an example of an area.  The story is supposed to focus on the parents, but it's more garbled than a radio signal out of range.  Nothing is explained, not even why the situation is there in the first place as the parents are just looking for symbols just because they're told things are dangerous.  And in the present era with the daughter, it's just useless filler cut off by a hidden object mission that makes no sense what-so-ever.  Furthermore, if I'm supposed to be looking for a mission object, then why do I need to collect all the other random junk?  Am I stealing to sell to a pawn shop for extra cash?  Don't expect the game to answer any of the questions it makes you think, you won't find any of them here.  Simply put, the story is rubbish.

In terms of mechanics, the game is decent-ish.  You can click a few times before the game penalizes you for a "mistake" and you can get "Gentle" and "I'll find everything myself" by replaying the same mission multiple times, but if you want "Racer", you need to 3 star 10 different missions (and no, asking for a hint does not penalize points if you're looking for 3 stars.  Use a hint if you're stuck, reload the map, and build up those combos).  Fortunately, energy is only taken from you for new missions.  Old missions can be replayed for free infinitely.  There's also some sort of "reward" for completing the missions in a set amount of time, but really it serves no purpose and is best ignored.  Additionally, the energy system makes no sense.  You're granted the exact number of energy to complete your levels in increments of 20...why not just give you simpler counts like one energy per level and with your cap at 5 instead of 100.  That's pretty much a more honest way to look at your energy.

You may end up irritated like me in the first hour and completion of this game takes about 3-4 hours.  Game can be completed for free, but you have to wait 45 minutes for each time you can try.  If you're looking for a relatively easy 100%, go right ahead and play this. But if you're looking for a fun time, then please consider looking elsewhere as I didn't find it here.

I'm writing this after completing all levels of the game. First, all levels were short and manageable, up to 14 objects iirc. Some items were also very cleverly hidden so there is a degree of challenge but not too difficult that I feel like my eyes want to tear from staring fixatedly at the screen for too long a duration.

The energy bar kinda makes sense and fits the theme. MCs travelling through time and they probably need to recharge, lol. I didn't mind the cooldown after every 5 levels since I was playing it casually.

Despite the setting and mystery surrounding the symbols, there is not much of a story. Storyline is very loose and scenes felt repetitive. Char sends text message to another char, then boom! you're in a particular environment. Start finding that hidden symbol. So goes the pattern for most of the levels. I love the visuals in this game and wish the story was better written.

As much as I'm a fan of icons replacing text in the interface navigation, I wish there was at least a small hover text that tells me what the symbol is for. Yes, I could have clicked to find out for myself, which I did eventually. 

For example, in every level, there are 3 challenges. 
First is finding all hidden objects, regardless whether a hint was used, you get a star for this first challenge.
Second is the time trial which involves finding all objects within a time limit.
The third challenge - after completing the game, I still have no clue what this 3rd challenge was even though in certain levels, I find I got a star for it. So yes, hover text would be helpful here.

Recommended for casual playing and to experience the beautiful visuals and BGM fitting each environment. Not recommended if you're looking to immerse in a story driven hidden object game.
